title: Alcaraz Is Back and Better Than Ever at the US Open!
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz is back on the tennis court — and he's playing awesome! The 23-year-old from Spain just won his third match at the US Open, beating China's Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1. That means he's through to the fourth round!

What makes this so cool? Alcaraz hurt his wrist in April and didn't play a singles match for 139 days. That's a really long time! His first match back was at this tournament, and now he's already winning in straight sets.

"To be honest, I'm better than I thought," Alcaraz said. "Right now, I think my level is really good. I think I have caught the rhythm of the competition."

He's won 17 matches in a row at big tournaments (called Grand Slams). He won the US Open in 2025 and the Australian Open in 2026. Now he wants to win the US Open again!

Some other top players have already lost, which makes it easier for Alcaraz. The world's number one player, Jannik Sinner, is injured and not playing. Novak Djokovic lost in the first round — a big surprise! And Felix Auger-Aliassime also lost early.

Next up for Alcaraz is Tommy Paul from the United States. Alcaraz has beaten Paul six times in a row, so he's feeling confident.

Alcaraz is called a "seven-time major champion" because he's won seven big tournaments. If he wins this one, it'll be his eighth! He says he's getting better with every match. Watch out, everyone — Alcaraz is on a mission!
why_it_matters: Alcaraz's comeback is a reminder that when you get knocked down by an injury or a setback, you can build yourself back up with time and hard work.
